newsitem.title: USA: Testimony ends in U.S. sergeant's rape trial.
newsitem.headline: Testimony ends in U.S. sergeant's rape trial.

text.p: Testimony ended Tuesday in the rape trial of Army Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson, clearing the way for final arguments in the case Wednesday.

Simpson's lawyers rested their case, in which they sought to show that all his sexual encounters with female trainees were consensual, after defence witnesses testified two of his alleged victims had said their sexual encounters were unpleasant.

Army Spec. Hannah Pitt, describing a conversation with one of the trainees Simpson is alleged to have raped, told the court: "(Rape) wasn't actually said, but when she was talking to me about it, it wasn't a happy feeling. The way I was talking to her I had to drag it out of her," she said.
Pitt had previously told investigators the trainee and Simpson had had consensual sex.

Simpson, 32, is charged with 19 counts of rape involving six women, and with 35 other counts including indecent exposure, battery and maltreatment. He has pleaded innocent to those charges but has admitted 11 counts of improper sexual intercourse with trainees and five of propositioning.
Simpson's lawyers have argued that all of Simpson's sexual encounters reflected an atmosphere of wanton sexual activity at the Army's Ordnance Centre and School, part of the Aberdeen Proving Ground.

After the defence rested, the prosecution concluded its case with the presentation of two rebuttal witnesses. A military jury is expected to begin deliberations on the Simpson case following closing arguments Wednesday and instructions to the six-member military jury.
Capt. Scott Alexander, who oversaw Simpson and other drill sergeants at the ordnance centre, testified Tuesday that he had no explanation for being unaware of sexual misconduct there.
"It's very disturbing to me that such events have occurred," he said. "It's beyond me why there was not any inkling whatsoever to any of the misconduct conditions."

Army Judge Col. Paul Johnston said, in a discussion with lawyers outside of the jurors' presence, that official ordnance centre policy encouraging an open atmosphere for reporting sexual harassment apparently was ignored.
"The culture within the unit was that they didn't report" (violations), he said.

Also testifying Tuesday, Pvt. Donna Jackson said the trainee Pitt had testified about had sex with Simpson more than once. But she also acknowledged, under cross-examination from prosecutor Capt. Theresa Gallagher, that the woman tried to warn others about drill sergeants at the facility.
"She was also warning you about the drill sergeants, that they did cruddy things to people?" Gallagher said.
Referring to a conversation with the woman regarding an encounter with Simpson, Jackson said, "She didn't say 'rape' to me when I spoke to her that night, but she was angry towards him (Simpson)."

E-4 Tamila Carrington, who acknowledged having sex with Simpson, testified that an alleged rape victim was laughing about her sexual experience with Simpson. Carrington said she reunited with her Aberdeen friend a year later.
Carrington said she believed that if her friend was raped, she would have told her.
Simpson is the first of 12 trainers at the proving ground charged with sexual misconduct to go to trial, although four other cases have been resolved through plea agreements or administrative means.
